title.en: Volume 40 Biographies 32: Wei Chiyun; Wang Gui; Yuwen Xiaoju; Yuwen Xiaobo; Yan Zhiyi
title.raw: 卷40 列傳第32 尉遲運 王軌 宇文神舉 宇文孝伯 顏之儀 Volume 40 Biographies 32: Wei Chiyun; Wang Gui; Yuwen Xiaoju; Yuwen Xiaobo; Yan Zhiyi

sentences.zh: 尉遲運 王軌 宇文神舉 宇文孝伯 顏之儀 樂運

translations.literal: Yuchi Yun, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, Yuwen Xiaobo, Yan Zhiyi, Yue Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yuchi Yun, Wang Gui, Yuwen Shenju, Yuwen Xiaobo, Yan Zhiyi, and Yue Yun.

sentences.zh: 王軌，太原祁人也，小名沙門，漢司徒允之後。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was a man of Qi in Taiyuan; childhood name Somen; descendant of Minister over the Masses Yun of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui came from Qi in Taiyuan; his childhood name was Somen; he was descended from Minister over the Masses Yun of Han.

sentences.zh: 世為州郡冠族。

translations.literal: For generations a commandery and prefecture leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been a leading house in their region.

sentences.zh: 累葉仕魏，賜姓烏丸氏。

translations.literal: Accumulated generations served Wei; granted surname Wuhuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: For many generations they served Wei and were granted the surname Wuhuan.

sentences.zh: 父光，少雄武，有將帥才略。

translations.literal: Father Guang — from youth fierce and martial; had general and commander talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang was fierce and martial from youth and possessed the talents of a commander.

sentences.zh: 每從征討，頻有戰功。

translations.literal: Each time following campaigns and punitive expeditions, repeatedly had battle achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he joined campaigns, he won repeated battlefield honors.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其勇決，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor knew his courage and decisiveness; treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai recognized his courage and resolution and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 位至驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、平原縣公。

translations.literal: Office reached Fast Cavalry Grand General, Opening-Office Equal in Three Departments, Duke of Pingyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to fast cavalry grand general, opening-office equal in three departments, and duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 軌性質直，慷慨有遠量。

translations.literal: Gui by nature straightforward in quality, generous and had far-reaching measure.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was blunt and upright by nature, generous-spirited, and far-seeing.

sentences.zh: 臨事強正，人不敢干。

translations.literal: Facing affairs forceful and upright; people dared not approach or interfere.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was forceful and upright, and none dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 起家事輔城公。

translations.literal: From family rise served Duke of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career in the household of the Duke of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 及高祖卽位，授前侍下士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoyu ascended, granted former attendant lower gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoyu took the throne, Gui was made a lower gentleman of the former attendants.

sentences.zh: 俄轉左侍上士，頗被識顧。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to left attendant upper gentleman; considerably received recognition and regard.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to upper gentleman of the left attendants and came under marked favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷內史上士、內史下大夫，加授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Accumulated promotions to palace scribe upper gentleman, palace scribe lower grand master; added grant Equal in Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to upper gentleman and then lower grand master in the palace scribe service, and was given the added rank of equal in three departments.

sentences.zh: 自此親遇彌重，遂處腹心之任。

translations.literal: From this personal encounter increasingly heavy; thereupon placed in heart-and-belly entrusted office.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he enjoyed ever closer trust and was entrusted with inner-circle duties.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護專政，高祖密欲圖之。

translations.literal: At the time Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu monopolized government; Emperor Xiaoyu secretly wished to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu dominated the government, Emperor Xiaoyu secretly planned to move against him.

sentences.zh: 以軌沉毅有識度，堪屬以大事，遂問以可否。

translations.literal: Because Gui was deep, resolute, and possessed knowledge and measure, able to entrust with great affairs — thereupon asked whether feasible or not.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Gui was grave, resolute, and farsighted enough to be trusted with a grave matter, the emperor asked his view.

sentences.zh: 軌贊成之。

translations.literal: Gui approved and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui gave his approval.

sentences.zh: 建德初，轉內史中大夫，加授開府儀同三司，又拜上開府儀同大將軍，封上黃縣公，邑一千戶，軍國之政，皆參預焉。

translations.literal: Early Jiande, transferred to palace scribe middle grand master; added grant Opening-Office Equal in Three Departments; again invested Upper Opening-Office Equal-in-Three-Departments Grand General; enfeoffed Duke of Shanghuang county, fief one thousand households; army-and-state government — all participated in.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiande he became middle grand master in the palace scribe service, was given opening-office equal in three departments, then appointed upper opening-office equal-in-three-departments grand general and enfeoffed duke of Shanghuang with a fief of one thousand households, taking part in both civil and military policy.

sentences.zh: 五年，高祖總戎東伐，六軍圍晉州。

translations.literal: Fifth year, Emperor Xiaoyu commanded troops in eastern punitive expedition; six armies besieged Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Emperor Xiaoyu took command of an eastern campaign, and the six armies laid siege to Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史崔景嵩守城北面，夜中密遣送款。

translations.literal: Inspector Cui Jingsong defended city north face; in night secretly sent surrender pledge.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector Cui Jingsong held the north side of the city and by night secretly sent word of surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔令軌率眾應之，未明，士皆登城鼓噪。

translations.literal: Imperial order commanded Gui lead masses to respond; before dawn, soldiers all climbed city and beat drums and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gui to lead troops to meet him; before dawn his men had scaled the walls with drums and shouting.

sentences.zh: 齊人駭懼，因卽退走。

translations.literal: Qi people alarmed and fearful; thereupon immediately retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi forces were stunned and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 遂克晉州，擒其城主特進、海昌王尉相貴，俘甲士八千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon captured Jin Province; seized its city lord specially advanced, Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui; captured armored soldiers eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Province fell; its defender, the specially advanced Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui, was taken, along with eight thousand armored troops.

sentences.zh: 於是遂從平幷、鄴。

translations.literal: Thereupon then followed pacification of Bing and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then took part in the conquest of Bing and Ye.

sentences.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，進爵郯國公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: By merit advanced office to Upper Grand General; advanced enfeoffment to Duke of Tan State, fief three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to upper grand general and raised to duke of Tan with a fief of three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及陳將吳明徹入寇呂梁，徐州總管梁士彥頻與戰不利，乃退保州城，不敢復出。

translations.literal: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Liang; Xuzhou area commander Liang Shiyan repeatedly battled not favorable; thereupon retreated to protect province city; dared not again go out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Liang, the Xuzhou area commander Liang Shiyan fought him repeatedly without success, withdrew into the provincial capital, and dared not emerge again.

sentences.zh: 明徹遂堰清水以灌之，列船艦於城下，以圖攻取。

translations.literal: Mingche thereupon dammed Clear Water to flood it; arrayed ships and warships below city; to plot attack and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche dammed the Qing River to flood the city and lined ships beneath the walls, intending to take it by assault.

sentences.zh: 詔以軌為行軍總管，率諸軍赴救。

translations.literal: Edict made Gui mobile campaign commander; led all armies to rush to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was appointed mobile campaign commander and sent at the head of relief armies.

sentences.zh: 軌潛於清水入淮口，多豎大木，以鐵鎖貫車輪，橫截水流，以斷其船路。

translations.literal: Gui secretly at Clear Water entering Huai mouth; many erected great trees; with iron chains pierced cart wheels; horizontally blocked water flow; to cut off their ship road.
translations.idiomatic: Gui quietly took up position where the Qing River enters the Huai, drove in many great posts, threaded iron chains through cart wheels, and strung them across the current to block the enemy fleet.

sentences.zh: 方欲密決其堰以斃之，明徹知之，懼，乃破堰遽退，冀乘決水之勢，以得入淮。

translations.literal: Just about to secretly breach their dam to drown them; Mingche knew it; fearful; thereupon broke dam hurriedly retreated; hoped ride breach-water momentum to attain enter Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Gui planned secretly to burst the dam and trap the enemy, Mingche learned of it in alarm, broke the dam himself, and fled downstream, hoping the rush of released water would carry him into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 比至清口，川流已闊，水勢亦衰，船艦竝礙於車輪，不復得過。

translations.literal: When reached Clear Mouth, river flow already broad; water momentum also declined; ships and warships together obstructed at cart wheels; no longer able pass.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the Qing mouth the channel had widened, the current had slackened, and every ship snagged on the chained wheels and could go no farther.

sentences.zh: 軌因率兵圍而蹙之。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon led troops surround and press upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then closed in with his troops and hemmed them in.

sentences.zh: 唯有騎將蕭摩訶以二千騎先走，得免。

translations.literal: Only cavalry general Xiao Mohe with two thousand horse first fled; attained escape.
translations.idiomatic: Only the cavalry commander Xiao Mohe escaped ahead with two thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 明徹及將士三萬餘人，幷器械輜重，竝就俘獲。

translations.literal: Mingche and officers and soldiers thirty thousand odd men; together with weapons and baggage train; together attained capture.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche, more than thirty thousand officers and men, and all their arms and supplies were taken captive.

sentences.zh: 陳之銳卒，於是殲焉。

translations.literal: Chen's sharp soldiers — at this annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Chen army's elite was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，進位柱國，仍拜徐州總管、七州十五鎮諸軍事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoyu praised it; advanced office Pillar of State; still invested Xuzhou area commander, seven provinces fifteen garrisons all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoyu commended him, raised him to pillar of state, and appointed him area commander of Xuzhou with authority over seven provinces and fifteen garrison commands.

sentences.zh: 軌性嚴重，多謀略，兼有呂梁之捷，威振敵境。

translations.literal: Gui by nature stern and grave, many stratagems; moreover had Liang victory; awe shook enemy borders.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and deliberate, rich in stratagem, and now crowned by victory at Liang, Gui's renown shook the enemy frontier.

sentences.zh: 陳人甚憚之。

translations.literal: Chen people greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen greatly dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝之征吐谷渾也，高祖令軌與宇文孝伯竝從，軍中進取，皆委軌等，帝仰成而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuandi's expedition against Tuyuhun; Emperor Xiaoyu ordered Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo together follow; in army advance and taking — all entrusted to Gui and others; Emperor merely looked upward to completion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuandi marched against Tuyuhun, Emperor Xiaoyu had Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo accompany him; all operational decisions were left to them while the emperor merely signed off.

sentences.zh: 時宮尹鄭譯、王端等竝得幸帝。

translations.literal: At the time palace directors Zheng Yi, Wang Duan and others together obtained Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The palace directors Zheng Yi and Wang Duan, among others, then enjoyed the emperor's special favor.

sentences.zh: 帝在軍中，頗有失德，譯等皆預焉。

translations.literal: Emperor in army, considerably had loss of virtue; Yi and others all participated therein.
translations.idiomatic: In camp the emperor behaved with notable impropriety, and Zheng Yi and the rest shared in it.

sentences.zh: 軍還，軌等言之於高祖。

translations.literal: Army returned; Gui and others spoke of it to Emperor Xiaoyu.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Gui and the others reported this to Emperor Xiaoyu.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，乃撻帝，除譯等名，仍加捶楚。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoyu greatly angry; thereupon flogged the heir; removed Yi and others from rolls; still added beating and scourging.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoyu flew into a rage, had the crown prince flogged, struck Zheng Yi and the rest from the rolls, and had them beaten as well.

sentences.zh: 帝因此大銜之。

translations.literal: The heir for this greatly harbored resentment toward them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince nursed a deep grudge over this.

sentences.zh: 軌又嘗與小內史賀若弼言及此事，且言皇太子必不克負荷。

translations.literal: Gui again once with junior palace scribe He Ruo Bi spoke of this matter; moreover said crown prince certainly could not bear burden.
translations.idiomatic: Gui once told the junior palace scribe He Ruo Bi about the affair and said the crown prince would surely fail to carry the burden.

sentences.zh: 弼深以為然，勸軌陳之。

translations.literal: Bi deeply took it as so; urged Gui state it.
translations.idiomatic: Bi agreed wholeheartedly and urged Gui to bring the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 軌後因侍坐，乃謂高祖曰：「皇太子仁孝無聞，復多涼德，恐不了陛下家事。

translations.literal: Gui later because attending seated, thereupon said to Emperor Xiaoyu: "Crown prince benevolence and filial piety not heard; moreover many cold virtues; fear cannot finish Your Majesty's household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while attending the emperor, Gui said to Emperor Xiaoyu, "The crown prince has shown no sign of benevolence or filial devotion, and his conduct has been shameful in many ways. I fear he cannot manage Your Majesty's house.

sentences.zh: 愚臣短暗，不足以論是非。

translations.literal: Foolish subject short and dark; not sufficient to discuss right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I am a dull and shortsighted subject, unfit to judge such matters.

sentences.zh: 陛下恆以賀若弼有文武奇才，識度宏遠，而弼比每對臣，深以此事為慮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty constantly because He Ruo Bi has civil and martial extraordinary talent, knowledge and measure broad and far; but Bi lately each time facing subject, deeply takes this matter as concern.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty always credits He Ruo Bi with rare civil and military gifts and a far-reaching mind, and Bi has lately confided to me that this weighs heavily on his thoughts.

sentences.zh: 」高祖召弼問之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaoyu summoned Bi and asked it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaoyu summoned Bi for questioning.

sentences.zh: 弼乃詭對曰：「皇太子養德春宮，未聞有過。

translations.literal: Bi thereupon deceptively replied: "Crown prince cultivating virtue in Eastern Palace; not heard has faults.
translations.idiomatic: Bi answered evasively, "The crown prince is being cultivated in the Eastern Palace, and I have heard no fault of him.

sentences.zh: 未審陛下，何從得聞此言？

translations.literal: Not examined Your Majesty — from where obtain hearing this speech?
translations.idiomatic: May I ask from whom Your Majesty heard such words?

sentences.zh: 」旣退，軌誚弼曰：「平生言論，無所不道，今者對揚，何得乃爾翻覆？

translations.literal: " After withdrawn, Gui reproached Bi: "Lifetime speech and discourse — nothing not spoken; today facing sovereign — how obtain thus flip-flop?
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward Gui rebuked Bi: "In private you say everything openly; before the throne today, why this sudden reversal?

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「此公之過也。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "This is lord's fault.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "That was your mistake.

sentences.zh: 皇太子，國之儲副，豈易攸言。

translations.literal: Crown prince — state's stored successor — how easily spoken of.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is the heir to the realm — not a thing one speaks of lightly.

sentences.zh: 事有蹉跌，便至滅門之禍。

translations.literal: Affair has stumble and fall; then reaches extermination of clan calamity.
translations.idiomatic: One misstep could bring ruin upon an entire house.

sentences.zh: 本謂公密陳臧否，何得遂至昌言。

translations.literal: Originally said lord secretly state good and bad; how obtain then reach open speech.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you would speak your mind in private — not proclaim it in open court.

sentences.zh: 」軌默然久之，乃曰：「吾專心國家，遂不存私計。

translations.literal: " Gui silent long; then said: "I single-mindedly state; do not preserve private plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui was silent a long while, then said, "My heart was fixed on the state alone; I gave no thought to my own safety.

sentences.zh: 向者對眾，良寔非宜。

translations.literal: Earlier facing the multitude — truly truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To have spoken so before the whole company was indeed ill judged.

sentences.zh: 」後軌因內宴上壽，又捋高祖須曰：「可愛好老公，但恨後嗣弱耳。

translations.literal: " Later Gui because inner feast offering longevity; again stroked Emperor Xiaoyu's beard saying: "Loveable good old lord — only regret successor weak.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, at a palace feast celebrating the emperor's birthday, Gui tugged Emperor Xiaoyu's beard and said, "You are a dear old man — I only wish your heirs were stronger.

sentences.zh: 」高祖深以為然。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaoyu deeply took it as so.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Xiaoyu agreed deeply.

sentences.zh: 但漢王次長，又不才，此外諸子竝幼，故不能用其說。

translations.literal: But Prince of Han second eldest, again without talent; beyond this all sons together young; therefore could not use his saying.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Prince of Han, though next in age, lacked ability too, and the other sons were still children, so the emperor could not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝卽位，追鄭譯等復為近侍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuandi ascended; pursued Zheng Yi and others restored as close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuandi took the throne, he recalled Zheng Yi and the rest to serve again at his side.

sentences.zh: 軌自知必及於禍，謂所親曰：「吾昔在先朝，寔申社稷至計。

translations.literal: Gui self knew certainly would reach calamity; said to intimate associates: "I formerly at former court truly stated altar-and-state supreme plan.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing retribution was inevitable, Gui told those close to him, "In the previous reign I spoke plainly for the good of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Today's affair — broken can be known.
translations.idiomatic: What will happen now is all too clear.

sentences.zh: 此州控帶淮南，鄰接強寇，欲為身計，易同反掌。

translations.literal: This province controls and belts Huainan; neighbors strong enemy; wishing act for self plan — easy as overturning palm.
translations.idiomatic: This province commands Huainan and borders a powerful foe; to scheme for my own survival would be as easy as turning my hand.

sentences.zh: 但忠義之節，不可虧違。

translations.literal: But loyalty and righteousness's integrity — cannot be diminished and violated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the code of loyalty and duty cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 況荷先帝厚恩，每思以死自效，豈以獲罪於嗣主，便欲背德於先朝。

translations.literal: Moreover burdened former emperor's thick grace; each thought with death self devote; how because receive crime from successor lord then wish betray virtue toward former court.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I owe the late emperor a deep debt and have always wished to repay it with my life; shall I turn faithless to the previous reign because the new sovereign condemns me?

sentences.zh: 止可於此待死，義不為他計。

translations.literal: Only can at here await death; righteousness not act other plan.
translations.idiomatic: I can only wait here for death; honor forbids any other course.

sentences.zh: 冀千載之後，知吾此心。」

translations.literal: Hope after a thousand years — know my this heart."
translations.idiomatic: I hope that ages hence someone will understand what moves me."

sentences.zh: 大象元年，帝令內史杜虔信就徐州殺軌。

translations.literal: First year of Daxiang; Emperor ordered palace scribe Du Qianxin go to Xuzhou kill Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In Daxiang year 1 the emperor sent the palace scribe Du Qianxin to Xuzhou to execute Gui.

sentences.zh: 御正中大夫顏之儀切諫，帝不納，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Proper Central upper grand master Yan Zhiyi fiercely remonstrated; Emperor did not accept; thereupon executed him.
translations.idiomatic: The proper central upper grand master Yan Zhiyi argued against it urgently, but the emperor would not listen and had Gui put to death.

sentences.zh: 軌立朝忠恕，兼有大功，忽以無罪被戮，天下知與不知，無不傷惜。

translations.literal: Gui standing at court loyal and forgiving; moreover had great merit; suddenly with no crime beheaded; under heaven know and not know — none not wounded and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had served loyally and with large-hearted integrity and had won great merit; his sudden execution on no charge moved all under heaven, acquainted or not, to grief.

sentences.zh: 宇文神舉，太祖之族子也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shenju — Grand Progenitor's clan son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju was a clansman of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 高祖晉陵、曾祖求男，仕魏，位竝顯達。

translations.literal: Great-great-grandfather Jinling, great-grandfather Qiuman — served Wei; offices both illustrious and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Jinling and great-grandfather Qiuman served Wei and both rose to notable rank.

sentences.zh: 祖金殿，魏鎮遠將軍、兗州刺史、安吉縣侯。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jindian — Wei General Who Pacifies the Distance, Inspector of Yan Province, Marquis of Anji county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jindian was a Wei general who pacifies the distance, inspector of Yan, and marquis of Anji.

sentences.zh: 父顯和，少而襲爵，性矜嚴，頗涉經史，膂力絕人，彎弓數百斤，能左右馳射。

translations.literal: Father Xianhe — from youth inherited enfeoffment; nature stern and strict; considerably crossed classics and histories; physical strength surpassed men; bent bow several hundred jin; able left and right gallop shoot.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianhe succeeded to the title while still young. Stern by nature and well read in the classics and histories, he had strength beyond ordinary men, could draw a bow of several hundred jin, and shoot with equal skill from either hand while riding.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武之在藩也，顯和早蒙眷遇。

translations.literal: When Wei Emperor Xiaowu was at fief, Xianhe early received favor and encounter.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was still a frontier prince, Xianhe won his early favor.

sentences.zh: 時屬多難，嘗問計於顯和。

translations.literal: Time belonged to many difficulties; once asked plan from Xianhe.
translations.idiomatic: In those troubled times the emperor once asked Xianhe for counsel.

sentences.zh: 顯和具陳宜杜門晦迹，相時而動。

translations.literal: Xianhe fully stated ought close doors and hide traces; watch time then move.
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe urged him plainly to withdraw from sight, bide his time, and act when the moment came.

sentences.zh: 孝武深納焉。

translations.literal: Xiaowu deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu took this advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，擢授冠軍將軍、合內都督，封城陽縣公，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When ascended throne; exceptionally appointed General Who Wins; combined inner area commander; enfeoffed Duke of Chengyang county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne he was promoted to general who wins, made combined inner area commander, and enfeoffed duke of Chengyang with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝武以顯和藩邸之舊，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Xiaowu because Xianhe fief-residence old associate; treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering their bond from the frontier days, Xiaowu treated Xianhe with great favor.

sentences.zh: 時顯和所居宅隘陋，乃撤殿省，賜為寢室。

translations.literal: At the time Xianhe's dwelling narrow and crude; thereupon demolished palace office; granted as bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianhe's house proved cramped, the emperor tore down part of the palace offices and gave him the space for his quarters.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Thus seen and valued.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武專政，帝每不自安。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan monopolized government; Emperor each time not self at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gao Huan seized power, the emperor grew uneasy day by day.

sentences.zh: 謂顯和曰：「天下洶洶，將若之何？

translations.literal: Said to Xianhe: "Under heaven tumultuous and surging — will like what?
translations.idiomatic: He said to Xianhe, "The realm is in turmoil — what am I to do?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「當今之計，莫若擇善而從之。

translations.literal: " Replied: "Present plan — none like choose good then follow it.
translations.idiomatic: " Xianhe answered, "The best course now is to choose what is right and follow it.

sentences.zh: 」因誦詩雲：「彼美人兮，西方之人兮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon recited poem says: "That beautiful person — western region's person.
translations.idiomatic: " and quoted the ode: "That fair one — a man of the west.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「是吾心也。

translations.literal: " Emperor said: "This is my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "That is my own thought.

sentences.zh: 」遂定入關之策。

translations.literal: " Thereupon settled enter-Pass strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " and so the plan to enter Guanzhong was decided.

sentences.zh: 帝以顯和母老，家累又多，令預為計。

translations.literal: Emperor because Xianhe's mother old, family burdens also many; ordered beforehand make plan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xianhe's mother was elderly and his household large, the emperor told him to make arrangements in advance.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今日之事，忠孝不可並立。

translations.literal: Replied: "Today's affair — loyalty and filial piety cannot together stand.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In the present crisis loyalty and filial duty cannot both be satisfied.

sentences.zh: 然臣不密則失身，安敢預為私計。

translations.literal: Yet subject not secret then loses body; how dare beforehand make private plan.
translations.idiomatic: And if a minister is not discreet he risks his life — how could I make private plans beforehand?

sentences.zh: 」帝愴然改容曰：「卿卽我之王陵也。

translations.literal: " Emperor grieved changed countenance: "Lord — you are my Wang Ling.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's face changed with sorrow as he said, "You are my Wang Ling.

sentences.zh: 」遷朱衣直閤、閤內大都督，改封長廣縣公，邑一千五百戶。

translations.literal: " Transferred Crimson-Robe Direct Guard, Inside-Guard Great Area Commander; changed enfeoffment to Duke of Changguang county, fief one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made crimson-robe direct guard and great area commander of the inner guard, and his title was changed to duke of Changguang with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及高祖東伐，詔神舉從軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoyu eastern punitive expedition; edict Shenju follow army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoyu marched east, Shenju was ordered to accompany the campaign.

sentences.zh: 幷州平，卽授幷州刺史，加上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Bing Province pacified; immediately granted Bing Province inspector; added Upper Opening-Office Equal-in-Three-Departments Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bing Province was pacified he was made its inspector and given the added rank of upper opening-office equal-in-three-departments grand general.

sentences.zh: 州旣齊氏別都，控帶要重。

translations.literal: Province already Qi clan's secondary capital; controls and belts vital and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The province was the Qi dynasty's secondary capital and held a position of the first strategic importance.

sentences.zh: 平定甫爾，民俗澆訛，豪右之家，多為奸猾。

translations.literal: Peace had just been established; local custom was corrupt and depraved; powerful families were mostly cunning and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had order been restored when local mores turned lax; leading families were largely given to fraud and sharp dealing.

sentences.zh: 神舉勵精為治，示以威恩，旬月之間，遠邇悅服。

translations.literal: Shenju exerted himself in governance, showing authority and kindness; within ten days and a month, near and far were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju threw himself into administration, balancing sternness with grace, and within a month people near and far were won over.

sentences.zh: 尋加上大將軍，改封武德郡公，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Soon added as Grand General; changed enfeoffment to Duke of Wude commandery; fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the added rank of grand general, raised to duke of Wude commandery, and granted two thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 俄進柱國大將軍，改封東平郡公，增邑通前六千九百戶。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to Pillar-of-State Grand General; changed enfeoffment to Duke of Dongping commandery; fief with previous totaled six thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to pillar-of-state grand general, made duke of Dongping commandery, and his fief reached six thousand nine hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 所部東壽陽縣土人，相聚為盜，率其黨五千人，來襲州城。

translations.literal: Local people of Dongshouyang county in his jurisdiction gathered as bandits; leading their faction of five thousand men, they came to attack the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: The natives of Dongshouyang county in his district banded together as robbers and, at the head of five thousand followers, raided the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 神舉以州兵討平之。

translations.literal: Shenju with provincial troops suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju put them down with the provincial army.

sentences.zh: 初，神舉見待於高祖，遂處心腹之任。

translations.literal: At first Shenju was treated well by Emperor Xiaoyu and came to hold a trusted inner position.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Emperor Xiaoyu had shown him special favor, and he came to stand among the emperor's closest confidants.

sentences.zh: 王軌、宇文孝伯等屢言皇太子之短，神舉亦頗與焉。

translations.literal: Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others repeatedly spoke of the crown prince's faults; Shenju also took part somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others often criticized the crown prince, and Shenju joined them more than once.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝卽位，荒淫無度，神舉懼及於禍，懷不自安。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, dissolute beyond measure, Shenju feared disaster and was uneasy at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xuan took the throne and gave himself over to boundless excess, Shenju feared he would be caught up in ruin and could not feel secure.

sentences.zh: 初定范陽之後，威聲甚振。

translations.literal: After first pacifying Fanyang, his renown greatly shook.
translations.idiomatic: After he first pacified Fanyang his reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 帝亦忌其名望，兼以宿憾，遂使人齎鴆酒賜之，薨於馬邑。

translations.literal: The emperor also envied his fame; together with old resentment, he sent someone bearing poisoned wine to grant him; he died at Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented his standing as well as an old grudge and sent an envoy with poisoned wine; Shenju died at Mayi.

sentences.zh: 時年四十八。

translations.literal: He was forty-eight at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 神舉偉風儀，善辭令，博涉經史，性愛篇章，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: Shenju had a grand bearing, was skilled in speech, broadly versed in classics and histories, loved literary composition by nature, and was especially adept at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju was imposing in presence, eloquent, widely read in the classics and histories, fond of writing by temperament, and especially masterful on horseback with bow in hand.

sentences.zh: 臨戎對寇，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: Facing battle and confronting the foe, brave and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: In the field against the enemy he was bold and shrewd.

sentences.zh: 蒞職當官，每著聲績。

translations.literal: Holding office and serving in post, he always achieved renown and merit.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he won a name for solid achievement.

sentences.zh: 兼好施愛士，以雄豪自居。

translations.literal: He also loved to bestow favors and cherish scholars, holding himself as a bold hero.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous to men of talent and carried himself like a great champion.

sentences.zh: 故得任兼文武，聲彰中外。

translations.literal: Thus he held posts combining civil and military roles; his fame resounded within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore served in both civil and military capacities, and his reputation rang at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 百僚無不仰其風則，先輩舊齒至於今而稱之。

translations.literal: None among the hundred officials failed to look up to him as a model; elders of former days even to this day praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Every official looked up to him as a standard, and older contemporaries still speak of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 子同嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong inherited his place.

sentences.zh: 位至儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Reached the rank of Equal-in-Protocol Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to equal-in-protocol grand general.

sentences.zh: 神舉弟神慶，少有壯志，武藝絕倫。

translations.literal: Shenju's younger brother Shenqing from youth had bold ambition; martial skill unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju's younger brother Shenqing had been ambitious from boyhood and was without peer in arms.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至柱國、汝南郡公。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, reached Pillar-of-State and Duke of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he had become a pillar-of-state and duke of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 建德之後，皇太子稍長，旣無令德，唯昵近小人。

translations.literal: After Jiande, the crown prince had grown somewhat; lacking fine virtue, he only drew near to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiande era the crown prince was no longer young, yet showed little worthy conduct and kept company only with base favorites.

sentences.zh: 孝伯白高祖曰：「皇太子四海所屬，而德聲未聞。

translations.literal: Xiaobo told Emperor Xiaoyu: "The crown prince is what the Four Seas look to, yet no report of his virtue is heard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Xiaobo told Emperor Xiaoyu, "The crown prince is the hope of the realm, yet we hear nothing of his moral reputation.

sentences.zh: 臣忝宮官，寔當其責。

translations.literal: I, though unworthy, am a palace official, and truly should bear the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy to serve in the palace, but the duty is mine.

sentences.zh: 且春秋尚少，志業未成，請妙選正人，為其師友，調護聖質，猶望日就月將。

translations.literal: Moreover his years are still young, aspiration and achievement not yet formed; please finely select upright men as his teachers and friends, to nurture and guard the holy quality, still hoping he improves day by day and month by month.
translations.idiomatic: He is still young and his character is not yet formed. Please choose worthy men as his teachers and companions to cultivate his nature, so that he may grow better day by day and month by month.

sentences.zh: 如或不然，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: If it be not so, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If that is not done, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 」帝斂容曰：「卿世載鯁直，竭誠所事。

translations.literal: " The emperor composed his expression and said: "Your family for generations bears straight integrity; you serve with full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew grave and said, "Your house has been upright for generations, and you serve with complete loyalty.

sentences.zh: 觀卿此言，有家風矣。

translations.literal: Seeing these words of yours, there is family style.
translations.idiomatic: From what you say, I see the spirit of your family.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯拜謝曰：「非言之難，受之難也。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo bowed in thanks and said: "It is not speech that is hard, but acceptance that is hard.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo bowed and replied, "The hard part is not speaking, but being heard.

sentences.zh: 深願陛下思之。

translations.literal: I deeply wish Your Majesty will ponder it.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly beg Your Majesty to weigh this.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「正人豈復過君。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Could an upright man surpass you?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Where would I find an upright man better than you?

sentences.zh: 」於是以尉遲運為右宮正，孝伯仍為左宮正。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yuchi Yun was made Right Palace Tutor; Xiaobo remained as Left Palace Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yuchi Yun was appointed right palace tutor and Xiaobo remained left palace tutor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜宗師中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Middle Grand Master of the Preceptorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made middle grand master of the preceptorate.

sentences.zh: 及吐谷渾入寇，詔皇太子征之。

translations.literal: When Tuyuhun invaded, an edict ordered the crown prince to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the frontier, the crown prince was ordered to take the field against them.

sentences.zh: 軍中之事，多決於孝伯。

translations.literal: Military affairs in the army were mostly decided by Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Most decisions in the campaign were left to Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 俄授京兆尹，入為左宮伯，轉右宮伯。

translations.literal: Soon granted as Governor of Jingzhao; entered service as Left Palace Tutor; transferred to Right Palace Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Jingzhao, then served as left palace tutor and was transferred to right palace tutor.

sentences.zh: 嘗因侍坐，帝問之曰：「我兒比來漸長進不？

translations.literal: Once while attending seated, the emperor asked him: "Has my son lately been gradually improving?
translations.idiomatic: Once, while Xiaobo was in attendance, the emperor asked, "Has my son been making progress lately?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「皇太子比懼天威，更無罪失。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The crown prince, lately fearing imperial majesty, has no more faults.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Lately the crown prince has been in awe of your majesty and has not repeated his faults.

sentences.zh: 」及王軌因內宴捋帝須，言太子之不善，帝罷酒，責孝伯曰：「公常語我，雲太子無過。

translations.literal: When Wang Gui at an inner banquet pulled the emperor's beard and spoke of the crown prince's ill conduct, the emperor ended the feast and rebuked Xiaobo: "You always tell me that the crown prince has no faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gui at a private banquet seized the emperor's beard and spoke of the crown prince's misconduct, the emperor broke off the feast and rebuked Xiaobo: "You always tell me the crown prince has done no wrong.

sentences.zh: 今軌有此言，公為誑矣。

translations.literal: Now Gui has these words—you have deceived me.
translations.idiomatic: Now Gui says this—you have misled me.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯再拜曰：「臣聞父子之際，人所難言。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo bowed again and said: "I have heard that between father and son, what men find hardest to speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo bowed again and said, "Between father and son there are things men find hardest to say.

sentences.zh: 臣知陛下不能割情忍愛，遂爾結舌。

translations.literal: I know Your Majesty cannot sever affection and restrain love, and so I held my tongue.
translations.idiomatic: I knew Your Majesty could not bear to cut off affection, and so I kept silent.

sentences.zh: 」帝知其意，默然久之，乃曰：「朕已委公矣，公其勉之。」

translations.literal: " The emperor knew his meaning, was silent long, then said: "I have already entrusted this to you; exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor understood, was silent a long while, then said, "I have already entrusted this to you. Do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 五年，大軍東討，拜內史下大夫，令掌留台事。

translations.literal: In year 5, the great army campaigned east; appointed Under Director of the Internal Secretary, ordered to manage affairs of the capital in the emperor's absence.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, when the main army marched east, he was made under director of the internal secretary and charged with running the capital in the emperor's absence.

sentences.zh: 軍還，帝曰：「居守之重，無忝戰功。

translations.literal: Army returned; the emperor said: "The weight of holding the capital—no disgrace to battle merit."
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor said, "You held the capital well—your service matched the fighting merit."

sentences.zh: 」於是加授大將軍，進爵廣陵郡公，邑三千戶，幷賜金帛及女妓等。

translations.literal: Thereupon added as Grand General; advanced in rank to Duke of Guangling commandery, fief three thousand households; and together granted gold, silk, and female entertainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given the added rank of grand general, raised to duke of Guangling with a fief of three thousand households, and rewarded with gold, silk, and female entertainers.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為宗師。

translations.literal: Year 6, again made Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was again made preceptor.

sentences.zh: 每車駕巡幸，常令居守。

translations.literal: Each time the imperial carriage toured, he was always ordered to remain and hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled, Xiaobo was left behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 其後高祖北討，至雲陽宮，遂寢疾。

translations.literal: After this Emperor Xiaoyu campaigned north; reaching Yunyang Palace, he then fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Emperor Xiaoyu marched north and reached Yunyang Palace, he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 驛召孝伯赴行在所。

translations.literal: By relay post he summoned Xiaobo to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Xiaobo by fast courier to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 帝執其手曰：「吾自量必無濟理，以後事付君。

translations.literal: The emperor took his hand and said: "I myself measure that I surely cannot be cured; I entrust later affairs to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand and said, "I know I cannot recover. I leave what follows to you.

sentences.zh: 」是夜，授司衛上大夫，總宿衛兵馬事。

translations.literal: " That night, granted Senior Grand Master of the Palace Guard, overall charge of palace guard troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: " That same night he was made senior grand master of the palace guard with overall command of the palace troops.

sentences.zh: 又令馳驛入京鎮守，以備非常。

translations.literal: Also ordered him to ride relay post into the capital to hold guard, to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to ride posthaste to the capital and hold it against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，授小冢宰。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan succeeded; granted Lesser Household Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Xiaobo was made lesser household minister.

sentences.zh: 帝忌齊王憲，意欲除之。

translations.literal: The emperor envied Prince of Qi Xian, wishing to eliminate him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and wanted him removed.

sentences.zh: 謂孝伯曰：「公能為朕圖齊王，當以其官位相授。

translations.literal: He told Xiaobo: "If you can plot Qi Wang for me, I shall give you his offices and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xiaobo, "If you will help me destroy the Prince of Qi, I will give you his offices and rank.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯叩頭曰：「先帝遺詔，不許濫誅骨肉。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo knocked his head and said: "The late emperor's testamentary edict forbids wanton execution of kin.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo kowtowed and said, "The late emperor's testament forbade the reckless killing of royal kin.

sentences.zh: 齊王，陛下之叔父，戚近功高，社稷重臣，棟樑所寄。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's paternal uncle, kin near and merit high, a weighty minister of the altars of state, in whom the beam and pillar are entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's uncle, a close kinsman of high merit and a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下若妄加刑戮，微臣又順旨曲從，則臣為不忠之臣，陛下為不孝之子也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty rashly add punishment and execution, and this humble minister again follow the intent and bend compliance, then I would be an unfaithful minister and Your Majesty an unfilial son.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty kills him without cause and I go along, I shall be disloyal and Your Majesty unfilial.

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌，因漸疎之。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased, and for this gradually kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took offense and gradually estranged him.

sentences.zh: 乃與于智、王端、鄭譯等密圖其事。

translations.literal: He then with Yu Zhi, Wang Duan, Zheng Yi, and others secretly plotted the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly plotted with Yu Zhi, Wang Duan, Zheng Yi, and others.

sentences.zh: 後令智告憲謀逆，遣孝伯召憲入，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Later he had Zhi accuse Xian of plotting rebellion; sent Xiaobo to summon Xian in, then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he had Yu Zhi accuse Xian of treason, sent Xiaobo to summon him to court, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 帝之西征也，在軍有過行，鄭譯時亦預焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned west, there were lapses in conduct in the army; Zheng Yi at the time also took part.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign the crown prince, later Emperor Xuan, had behaved badly in camp, and Zheng Yi had joined in.

sentences.zh: 軍還，孝伯及王軌盡以白，高祖怒，撻帝數十，仍除譯名。

translations.literal: Army returned; Xiaobo and Wang Gui fully reported them; Emperor Xiaoyu was furious, flogged the emperor several tens of strokes, and moreover removed Yi's name from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Xiaobo and Wang Gui reported everything; Emperor Xiaoyu was furious, flogged the crown prince dozens of times, and stripped Zheng Yi of office.

sentences.zh: 至是，譯又被帝親昵。

translations.literal: At this time, Yi again was favored and intimate with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zheng Yi had again become a favorite of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝旣追憾被杖，乃問譯曰：「我腳上杖痕，誰所為也？

translations.literal: The emperor, brooding over resentment at being flogged, then asked Yi: "The cane marks on my shins—who made them?
translations.idiomatic: Brooding over the beating, the emperor asked Zheng Yi, "Who left the cane marks on my legs?

sentences.zh: 」譯答曰：「事由宇文孝伯及王軌。

translations.literal: " Yi answered: "The matter arose from Yuwen Xiaobo and Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Yi answered, "It was Yuwen Xiaobo and Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 」譯又因說王軌捋須事。

translations.literal: Yi moreover spoke again of Wang Gui pulling the beard incident.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi also brought up Wang Gui's pulling the emperor's beard.

sentences.zh: 帝乃誅軌。

translations.literal: The emperor then executed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then had Wang Gui executed.

sentences.zh: 尉遲運懼，私謂孝伯曰：「吾徒必不免禍，為之奈何？

translations.literal: Yuchi Yun was afraid; privately he told Xiaobo: "Our kind surely cannot escape disaster—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yun was frightened and said privately to Xiaobo, "Our sort will surely not escape harm. What can we do?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯對曰：「今堂上有老母，地下有武帝，為臣為子，知欲何之。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo replied: "Now above the hall there is an old mother; below the ground there is the Martial Emperor. As minister and as son—where would one wish to go?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo replied, "I have an old mother above and the late Emperor Xiaoyu below. As minister and as son, where could I go?

sentences.zh: 且委質事人，本狥名義，諫而不入，將焉逃死。

translations.literal: Moreover, having pledged one's body to serve another, one originally dies for name and righteousness; if remonstrance is not heeded, where can one flee from death?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, once you have pledged yourself to serve, you live and die for duty. If remonstrance fails, death is the only course left.

sentences.zh: 足下若為身計，宜且遠之。

translations.literal: If you, sir, take thought for yourself, you should for the time draw away.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to save yourself, you had better keep your distance for now.

sentences.zh: 」於是各行其志。

translations.literal: " Thereupon each followed his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: " After that each did as he thought best.

sentences.zh: 運尋出為秦州總管。

translations.literal: Yun soon went out as Area Commander of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yun was soon sent out as area commander of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 然帝荒淫日甚，誅戮無度，朝章弛紊，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor grew daily more dissolute, executions without limit, court regulations lax and tangled, no longer any discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor grew more dissolute by the day, killing without restraint until court order collapsed altogether.

sentences.zh: 孝伯又頻切諫，皆不見從。

translations.literal: Xiaobo again frequently remonstrated sharply; none was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 由是益疎斥之。

translations.literal: For this he was further kept at a distance and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was pushed farther away and cast aside.

sentences.zh: 後稽胡反，令孝伯為行軍總管，從越王盛討平之。

translations.literal: Later when the Ji Hu rebelled, he made Xiaobo campaign marshal and followed Prince of Yue Sheng to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji Hu rebelled later, Xiaobo was made campaign marshal and marched with Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng to put them down.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，帝將殺之，乃託以齊王之事，誚之曰：「公知齊王謀反，何以不言？

translations.literal: When the army returned, the emperor was about to kill him; he used the Qi Wang affair as pretext, reproached him: "You knew Qi Wang plotted rebellion—why did you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the emperor meant to kill him. Using the Prince of Qi as a pretext, he rebuked Xiaobo: "You knew the Prince of Qi was plotting rebellion—why did you say nothing?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯對曰：「臣知齊王忠於社稷，為羣小媒孽，加之以罪。

translations.literal: " Xiaobo replied: "I knew Prince of Qi was loyal to the altars of state; petty men slandered and harmed him, adding crime to him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo replied, "I knew the Prince of Qi was loyal to the state. Petty men slandered him and piled false charges upon him.

sentences.zh: 臣以言必不用，所以不言。

translations.literal: I reckoned speech would surely not be heeded, and so did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: I knew anything I said would be ignored, so I kept silent.

sentences.zh: 且先帝付囑微臣，唯令輔導陛下，今諫而不從，寔負顧托。

translations.literal: Moreover the late emperor entrusted charge to this humble minister, only ordering me to assist and guide Your Majesty; now remonstrance is not heeded—I truly fail the entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor entrusted me only to guide Your Majesty. Now that my remonstrance goes unheeded, I have failed that charge.

sentences.zh: 以此為罪，是所甘心。

translations.literal: To take this as crime—I gladly accept it.
translations.idiomatic: If that is my crime, I accept it willingly.

sentences.zh: 」帝大慚，俛首不語。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly ashamed, bowed his head and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was deeply ashamed and looked down without a word.

sentences.zh: 乃命將出，賜死于家。

translations.literal: Yet he ordered guards sent out, granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Even so he sent guards and had Xiaobo granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was thirty-six at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝踐極，以孝伯及王軌忠而獲罪，竝令收葬，復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, because Xiaobo and Wang Gui were faithful yet suffered punishment, together ordered them collected and buried, restoring their offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, he had Xiaobo and Wang Gui reburied with honor and their offices and ranks restored, because both had been loyal men punished unjustly.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂高熲曰：「宇文孝伯寔有周之良臣，若使此人在朝，我輩無措手處也。

translations.literal: He also once told Gao Jiong: "Yuwen Xiaobo was truly a good minister of Zhou; if this man had been in court, we would have had no room to act.
translations.idiomatic: He also once told Gao Jiong, "Yuwen Xiaobo was a true good minister of Zhou. If he had still been at court, we would have had no opening.

sentences.zh: 」子歆嗣。

translations.literal: " His son Xin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: " His son Xin inherited his place.

sentences.zh: 顏之儀字子升，琅邪臨沂人也，晉侍中含九世孫。

translations.literal: Yan Zhiyi, styled Zisheng, was a man of Linyi in Langye; ninth-generation descendant of Jin Attendant-in-Ordinary Yan Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiyi, courtesy name Zisheng, came from Linyi in Langye and was the ninth in descent from Yan Han, attendant-in-ordinary under Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖見遠，齊御史治書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jianyuan was Qi Director of the Censorate for Legal Text.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jianyuan had served Qi as director of the censorate for legal text.

sentences.zh: 正色立朝，有當官之稱。

translations.literal: Upright in countenance standing at court, he had the reputation of filling his office.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and upright at court, he was praised as a man who truly filled his post.

sentences.zh: 及梁武帝執政，遂以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took power, he then on grounds of illness resigned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang seized power, he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋而齊和帝暴崩，見遠慟哭而絕。

translations.literal: Soon Qi Emperor He suddenly died; Jianyuan wept in grief and expired.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qi Emperor He died suddenly; Jianyuan mourned until he collapsed and died.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝深恨之，謂朝臣曰：「我自應天從人，何預天下人事，而顏見遠乃至於此。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply resented this; he told court ministers: "I myself responded to Heaven and followed the people—what of the affairs of all under Heaven had I to do with it, that Yan Jianyuan should come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply resented it and told the court, "I merely answered Heaven and followed the people. What had Yan Jianyuan to do with the affairs of the realm that he should die like this?

sentences.zh: 」當時嘉其忠烈，咸稱歎之。

translations.literal: At the time they praised his loyal valor; all called it admirable and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time admired his loyalty and courage, and all spoke of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 父協，以見遠蹈義忤時，遂不仕進。

translations.literal: His father Xie, because Jianyuan embraced righteousness against the times, then did not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie, seeing that Jianyuan had chosen righteousness against the age, refused office thereafter.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝為湘東王，引協為其府記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang was Prince of Xiangdong, he recruited Xie as recording secretary in his princely household.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan was still Prince of Xiangdong, he brought Xie into his household as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 協不得已，乃應命。

translations.literal: Xie, having no choice, thereupon accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Left with no alternative, Xie finally accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝後著《懷舊志》及詩，並稱讚其美。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Yuan of Liang composed the "Records of Nostalgia for Old Friends" and poems, all praising his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Yuan of Liang wrote the Records of Nostalgia for Old Friends and poems, all commending Xie's virtue.

sentences.zh: 之儀幼穎悟，三歲能讀《孝經》。

translations.literal: Zhiyi in youth was quick and perceptive; at three years he could read the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhiyi was exceptionally bright; at three he could read the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉羣書，好為詞賦。

translations.literal: When grown, he broadly traversed all books and loved to compose fu poetry.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he read widely and delighted in writing fu verse.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《神州頌》，辭致雅贍。

translations.literal: Once he presented the "Ode to the Divine Land"; the wording was elegant and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted an "Ode to the Divine Land" with graceful, richly turned phrasing.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝手勑報曰：「枚乘二葉，俱得游梁；

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang by personal hand-edict replied saying: "Mei Sheng two generations, both able to travel to Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang wrote back in his own hand: "Two generations of the Mei family both found welcome in Liang;

sentences.zh: 應貞兩世，竝稱文學。

translations.literal: Ying Zhen two eras, together called men of letters."
translations.idiomatic: and two generations of Ying Zhen were alike renowned for literary learning."

sentences.zh: 我求才子，鯁慰良深。」

translations.literal: "I seek talented men — great consolation indeed."
translations.idiomatic: "In finding a man of talent, my honest joy runs very deep."

sentences.zh: 江陵平，之儀隨例遷長安。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Zhiyi according to precedent was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Zhiyi was relocated to Chang'an along with the other captives.

sentences.zh: 世宗以為麟趾學士，稍遷司書上士。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made him a Linzhi Hall scholar; he was gradually promoted to Director of Documents Upper Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming appointed him a Linzhi Hall scholar, and he gradually rose to director of documents upper gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高祖初建儲宮，盛選師傅，以之儀為侍讀。

translations.literal: When Grand Ancestor first established the Eastern Palace, he lavishly selected tutors and made Zhiyi tutor-reader.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first set up the crown prince's household, he carefully chose instructors and made Zhiyi one of the readers-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 太子後征吐谷渾，在軍有過行，鄭譯等竝以不能匡弼坐譴，唯之儀以累諫獲賞。

translations.literal: Later the crown prince campaigned against Tuyuhun; in the army he had improper conduct. Zheng Yi and others all because of inability to correct and assist sat under censure; only Zhiyi because of repeated remonstrance received reward.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince later campaigned against Tuyuhun and misbehaved in camp, Zheng Yi and others were punished for failing to guide him; only Zhiyi was rewarded for having remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 卽拜小宮尹，封平陽縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Immediately appointed Lesser Palace Governor, enfeoffed Baron of Pingyang county with fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made lesser palace governor, enfeoffed baron of Pingyang with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝卽位，遷上儀同大將軍、御正中大夫，進爵為公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, transferred to Upper Pillar of State Grand General, Direct Regular Grand Master, advanced in enfeoffment to duke, fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Zhiyi was promoted to upper pillar-of-state grand general and direct regular grand master, raised to duke, and his fief increased by one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 帝後刑政乖僻，昏縱日甚，之儀犯顏驟諫，雖不見納，終亦不止。

translations.literal: Later the emperor's punishments and government were perverse; reckless indulgence daily grew worse. Zhiyi, offending face, repeatedly remonstrated; though not accepted, in the end he also did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's justice grew erratic and his recklessness daily worse, Zhiyi spoke bluntly time after time; though the throne would not listen, he would not cease.

sentences.zh: 深為帝所忌。

translations.literal: Deeply was he resented by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to regard him with deep suspicion.

sentences.zh: 然以恩舊，每優容之。

translations.literal: Yet because of old favor, each time he was treated with lenient forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as an old associate he was still treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 及帝殺王軌，之儀固諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor killed Wang Gui, Zhiyi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor put Wang Gui to death, Zhiyi remonstrated firmly against it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲幷致之於法。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished also to bring him within the law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and meant to punish him as well.

sentences.zh: 後以其諒直無私，乃舍之。

translations.literal: Later because of his honest straightforwardness without private motive, he was released.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, knowing his candor was disinterested, the emperor let him go.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，劉昉、鄭譯等矯遺詔，以隋文帝為丞相，輔少主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others forged a testamentary edict, making Emperor Wen of Sui chancellor to assist the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan's death, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others forged a deathbed edict naming Yang Jian, later Emperor Wen of Sui, regent for the young emperor.

sentences.zh: 之儀知非帝旨，拒而弗從。

translations.literal: Zhiyi knew it was not the emperor's intent and refused, not following.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi knew this was not the late emperor's wish and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 昉等草詔署記，逼之儀連署。

translations.literal: Fang and the others drafted the edict and signature record, forcing Zhiyi jointly to sign.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang and the others drafted the edict and pressed Zhiyi to cosign it.

sentences.zh: 之儀厲聲謂昉等曰：「主上升遐，嗣子沖幼，阿衡之任，宜在宗英。

translations.literal: Zhiyi in stern voice said to Fang and the others: "The lord has ascended afar; the heir is young and tender. The burden of regency ought to lie with the outstanding of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi said sharply to Liu Fang and his allies: "The sovereign is dead and the heir is only a child. The regency belongs with the most worthy prince of the blood.

sentences.zh: 方今賢戚之內，趙王最長，以親以德，合膺重寄。

translations.literal: Now among the worthy and kin, the Prince of Zhao is eldest; by closeness and by virtue he ought to receive the weighty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Of the princes, Zhao is the eldest — by blood and by merit he should bear this grave responsibility.

sentences.zh: 公等備受朝恩，當思盡忠報國，奈何一旦欲以神器假人！

translations.literal: You gentlemen all fully received court favor; you ought to think of exhausting loyalty and repaying the state. Why in one morning wish to lend the imperial regalia to another!
translations.idiomatic: You have all received deep favor from the throne. You ought to serve the realm faithfully — why would you hand the dynasty to an outsider overnight?

sentences.zh: 之儀有死而已，不能誣罔先帝。

translations.literal: Zhiyi has only death — he cannot deceive and wrong the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die than dishonor the late emperor's will."

sentences.zh: 」於是昉等知不可屈，乃代之儀署而行之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Fang and the others knew he could not be bent and thereupon signed for Zhiyi and issued it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not be moved, Liu Fang and the others forged his signature and issued the edict.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝后索符璽，之儀又正色曰：「此天子之物，自有主者，宰相何故索之？

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wen of Sui sought the seals and regalia. Zhiyi again with upright countenance said: "These are the Son of Heaven's things; they naturally have their owner. Why does the chancellor seek them?
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian later demanded the imperial seals, Zhiyi again said sternly: "These belong to the emperor alone. By what right does a chancellor demand them?

sentences.zh: 」於是隋文帝大怒，命引出，將戮之，然以其民之望也，乃止。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Emperor Wen of Sui was greatly angry, ordered him led out, and was about to execute him; yet because of his standing among the people, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was furious and ordered him dragged out for execution, but spared him because of his reputation among the people.

sentences.zh: 出為西疆郡守。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Xijiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was banished to serve as administrator of Xijiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，詔徵還京師，進爵新野郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui tread the ultimate, an edict summoned him back to the capital and advanced his enfeoffment to Duke of Xinye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Jian took the throne, an edict recalled him to the capital and raised him to duke of Xinye.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，拜集州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang, appointed Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 5 he was appointed inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 在州清靜，夷夏悅之。

translations.literal: In the province, quiet and pure; barbarians and Chinese were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was calm and upright, and both the native population and tribal peoples were content.

sentences.zh: 明年代還，遂優遊不仕。

translations.literal: The next year he was replaced and returned, then idly wandered without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and thereafter lived at leisure without serving again.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，之儀隨例入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Zhiyi according to precedent entered court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaihuang year 10, Zhiyi came to court as custom required.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝望而識之，命引至御坐，謂之曰：「見危授命，臨大節而不可奪，古人所難，何以加卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui saw him from afar and recognized him, ordered him led to the imperial seat, and said to him: "Facing danger and giving one's life; facing great integrity and not being diverted — what the ancients found hard — how can I further honor you?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian recognized him at once, had him brought to the throne, and said: "To accept death in danger and stand firm at a grave moral test — virtues the ancients found hard — how can I reward you enough?

sentences.zh: 」乃賜錢十萬、米一百石。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted money one hundred thousand and rice one hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him one hundred thousand cash and one hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of Kaihuang year 11, at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: There was a collected works of ten scrolls circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works in ten scrolls circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 時京兆郡丞樂運亦以直言數諫於帝。

translations.literal: At the time the Chief Assistant of the Capital Area Command, Le Yun, also because of blunt speech repeatedly remonstrated to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Le Yun, chief assistant of the Capital Area command, also spoke bluntly and remonstrated with the emperor repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 運字承業，南陽淯陽人，晉尚書令廣之八世孫。

translations.literal: Yun, styled Chengye, was a man of Yuyang in Nanyang — eighth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yun, courtesy name Chengye, came from Yuyang in Nanyang and was an eighth-generation descendant of the Jin minister of works Guang.

sentences.zh: 祖文素，齊南郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wensu was Administrator of Nan commandery under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wensu had been administrator of Nan commandery under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 父均，梁義陽郡守。

translations.literal: His father Jun was Administrator of Yiyang commandery under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had served Liang as administrator of Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 運少好學，涉獵經史，而不持章句。

translations.literal: Yun from youth loved learning, traversed and hunted the classics and histories, yet did not hold to clause-and-phrase study.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yun loved learning and read broadly in the classics and histories without fixating on textual glosses.

sentences.zh: 年十五而江陵滅，運隨例遷長安。

translations.literal: At age fifteen Jiangling was extinguished; Yun according to precedent was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he was fifteen and Jiangling fell, Yun was moved to Chang'an like the other captives.

sentences.zh: 其親屬等多被籍，而運積年為人傭保，皆贖免之。

translations.literal: His kinsmen and others mostly were registered as slaves; Yun for accumulated years worked as hired laborer and bondsman, all ransoming and freeing them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his relatives had been enslaved; for years he hired himself out and paid off their redemption one by one.

sentences.zh: 又事母及寡嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: Moreover he served his mother and widowed sister-in-law with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He also cared for his mother and widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 由是以孝義聞。

translations.literal: From this he became known for filial piety and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Through this he won renown for filial piety and moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 梁故都官郎琅邪王澄美之，為次其行事，為《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: Former Liang Director of Justice Langya Wang Cheng admired him, arranged his conduct in sequence, and made a "Biography of Filial Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng of Langya, a former Liang director of justice, admired him, recorded his deeds, and wrote a Biography of Filial Righteousness about him.

sentences.zh: 性方直，未嘗求媚於人。

translations.literal: By nature square and upright, he never once sought to flatter people.
translations.idiomatic: Square and upright by nature, he never curried favor with anyone.

sentences.zh: 天和初，起家夏州總管府倉曹參軍，轉柱國府記室參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he first took office as Granary Bureau Adjutant in the Xia Province Area Command headquarters; transferred to Recording Adjutant in the Pillar of State's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianhe he entered service as granary bureau adjutant under the Xia Province area command, then became recording adjutant on a pillar-of-state's staff.

sentences.zh: 尋而臨淄公唐瑾薦為露門學士。

translations.literal: Before long Duke of Linzi Tang Jin recommended him as Loumen Gate scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Duke of Linzi Tang Jin recommended him as a Loumen Gate scholar.

sentences.zh: 前後犯顏屢諫高祖，多被納用。

translations.literal: Before and after he offended face and repeatedly remonstrated Grand Ancestor; many were accepted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he spoke bluntly to Emperor Wu, and much of what he said was heeded.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，除萬年縣丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, appointed Chief Assistant of Wannian county.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year 2 he was made chief assistant of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 抑挫豪右，號稱強直。

translations.literal: He suppressed and thwarted powerful families; he was called forcefully upright.
translations.idiomatic: He checked the great clans and was known for uncompromising firmness.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，特許通籍，事有不便於時者，令巨細奏聞。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor praised him, specially permitted registry access; when affairs were not convenient to the times, ordered whether great or small to be memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu approved, gave him special access to court, and ordered him to report any matter great or small that harmed the public good.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗幸同州，召運赴行在所。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor once visited Tong Province and summoned Yun to the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Emperor Wu visited Tong Province he summoned Le Yun to his traveling court.

sentences.zh: 旣至，高祖謂運曰：「卿來日見太子不？

translations.literal: When arrived, Grand Ancestor said to Yun: "Did you on the way see the crown prince or not?
translations.idiomatic: When Yun arrived, Emperor Wu asked: "Did you see the crown prince on your way here?

sentences.zh: 」運曰：「臣來日奉辭。

translations.literal: " Yun said: "Your subject on the way came to take leave."
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered: "On the way I stopped to pay my respects to him."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「卿言太子何如人？

translations.literal: " Grand Ancestor said: "You say — what sort of man is the crown prince?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked: "What kind of man do you find the crown prince?

sentences.zh: 」運曰：「中人也。

translations.literal: " Yun said: "A middling man."
translations.idiomatic: Yun replied: "A man of middling capacity."

sentences.zh: 」時齊王憲以下，並在帝側。

translations.literal: " At the time Prince of Qi Xian and those below were all at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian and the other princes were all standing beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 高祖顧謂憲等曰：「百官佞我，皆雲太子聰明睿知，唯運獨雲中人，方驗運之忠直耳。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor turned and said to Xian and the others: "The hundred officers flatter me — all say the crown prince is clever and wise; only Yun alone says middling man. Just now we verify Yun's loyal uprightness."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu turned to Yuwen Xian and the others and said: "My officials all flatter me and call the crown prince brilliant; only Yun dares call him middling — that is proof of his honesty."

sentences.zh: 」於是因問運中人之狀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he then asked Yun the appearance of a middling man.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Yun what he meant by a middling man.

sentences.zh: 運對曰：「班固以齊桓公為中人，管仲相之則霸，豎貂輔之則亂。

translations.literal: Yun replied saying: "Ban Gu regarded Duke Huan of Qi as a middling man — with Guan Zhong as chancellor he then hegemonized; with Shu Diao as aide he then fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yun answered: "Ban Gu called Duke Huan of Qi a middling ruler — under Guan Zhong he became hegemon; under Shu Diao he brought chaos.

sentences.zh: 謂可與為善，亦可與為惡也。

translations.literal: It means one may do good with him, also may do evil with him."
translations.idiomatic: That is to say, he can be led toward good or toward evil."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「我知之矣。

translations.literal: " Grand Ancestor said: "I understand it now."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: "I take your point."

sentences.zh: 」遂妙選宮官，以匡弼之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he finely selected palace officers to correct and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: He then carefully chose palace tutors to guide the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 仍超拜運京兆郡丞。

translations.literal: Still further he was promoted beyond rank to Chief Assistant of the Capital Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yun was further promoted to chief assistant of the Capital Area command.

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: The crown prince heard it; his mind was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince heard of this he was deeply offended.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，宣帝嗣位。

translations.literal: When Grand Ancestor died, Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu's death, Emperor Xuan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，詔天下公除。

translations.literal: When the burial ended, an edict ordered the realm's public removal of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Once the funeral rites were complete, he ordered the whole empire out of mourning.

sentences.zh: 帝及六宮，便議卽吉。

translations.literal: The emperor and the six palaces immediately deliberated immediate auspicious [dress].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the inner palace at once planned to resume normal dress and rites.

sentences.zh: 運上疏曰：「三年之喪，自天子達于庶人。

translations.literal: Yun submitted a memorial saying: "Three years of mourning — from the Son of Heaven down to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yun submitted a memorial: "Three years of mourning bind everyone, from the Son of Heaven to the common people.

sentences.zh: 先王制禮，安可誣之。

translations.literal: Former kings fixed rites — how can they be falsely wronged?
translations.idiomatic: The ritual codes left by the ancient kings cannot simply be set aside.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子七月而葬，以俟天下畢至。

translations.literal: In rites, the Son of Heaven is buried at seven months, to await all under Heaven fully arriving.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual the Son of Heaven is buried after seven months, so mourners from across the realm may arrive.

sentences.zh: 今葬期旣促，事訖便除，文軌之內，奔赴未盡；

translations.literal: Now the burial period is already pressed; when the affair ends then immediately removal — within the civilized realm, rushing to attend is not yet complete;
translations.idiomatic: The burial has already been rushed, and you now propose to end mourning immediately; within the empire many mourners have not yet arrived;

sentences.zh: 鄰境遠聞，使猶未至。

translations.literal: neighboring borders at distant hearing — envoys still have not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: and envoys from distant neighbors have not yet come.

sentences.zh: 若以喪服受弔，不可旣吉更凶；

translations.literal: If with mourning garments one receives condolence, one cannot having been auspicious again become inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: To receive condolences in mourning garb and then cast it off would turn auspicious rites back into inauspicious ones;

sentences.zh: 如以玄冠對使，未知此出何禮。

translations.literal: if with dark cap one faces envoys, I do not know from what rite this comes.
translations.idiomatic: to greet envoys in everyday dress has no basis in ritual that I know of.

sentences.zh: 進退無據，愚臣竊所未安。

translations.literal: Advance and retreat without basis — this foolish subject privately has never been at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Proceeding or withdrawing, there is no proper ground for either — your humble servant cannot be at ease.

sentences.zh: 」書奏，帝不納。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted; the emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rejected the memorial.

sentences.zh: 自是德政不修，數行赦宥。

translations.literal: From this virtuous government was not cultivated; repeatedly amnesties were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor neglected good governance and issued frequent pardons.

sentences.zh: 運又上疏曰：「臣謹案《周官》曰：『國君之過市，刑人赦。

translations.literal: Yun again submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject respectfully examines the Rites of Zhou, which says: 'When the ruler of the state passes the market, punishments and people are pardoned.'
translations.idiomatic: Le Yun memorialized again: "Your subject notes that the Rites of Zhou say: 'When the ruler passes through the market, punishments are remitted and prisoners released.'"

sentences.zh: 』此謂市者交利之所，君子無故不游觀焉。

translations.literal: " This means the market is where profit is exchanged; the gentleman without reason does not stroll and observe it.
translations.idiomatic: "That means the market is a place of profit-making — a gentleman does not visit it without good reason.

sentences.zh: 若游觀，則施惠以悅之也。

translations.literal: If he strolls and observes, then he bestows favor to please them.
translations.idiomatic: If he does go there, it is to show favor and please the people."

sentences.zh: 《尚書》曰：『眚災肆赦。
