translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: 'Calamities and disasters — broadly pardon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: 'When calamities occur, grant broad pardon.'"

sentences.zh: 』此謂過誤為害，罪雖大，當緩赦之。

translations.literal: " This means faults and mistakes that cause harm — though the crime be great, one ought leniently to pardon.
translations.idiomatic: "That refers to unintentional harm — even when the offense is grave, pardon should be considered.

sentences.zh: 呂刑云：『五刑之疑，有赦。

translations.literal: Lü xing says: 'When the five punishments are in doubt, there is pardon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Punishments of Lü says: 'When the five punishments are uncertain, there may be pardon.'"

sentences.zh: 』此謂

translations.literal: " This means
translations.idiomatic: "These passages mean

translations.literal: (赦) [emended: 刑]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: punishment]

sentences.zh: 〔刑〕疑從罰，罰疑從免。

translations.literal: [emended: 刑] when in doubt follows punishment; when punishment is in doubt follows acquittal.
translations.idiomatic: that when criminal guilt is uncertain, punishment still applies; when the penalty itself is uncertain, acquittal follows.

sentences.zh: 《論語》曰：『赦小過，舉賢才。

translations.literal: The Analects says: 'Pardon small faults; elevate talented men.'
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: 'Overlook petty offenses and promote the worthy.'"

sentences.zh: 』謹尋經典，未有罪無輕重，溥天大赦之文。

translations.literal: " Respectfully searching the classics, there is never text of crimes without light or heavy, universal-under-Heaven great pardon.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet nowhere in the classics do I find authority for indiscriminate, empire-wide amnesties regardless of the gravity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 逮茲末葉，不師古始，無益於治，未可則之。

translations.literal: Reaching this final age, not taking ancient beginnings as master — without benefit to government; not admissible as model.
translations.idiomatic: In these decadent times to abandon ancient precedent helps no one govern well, and ought not be imitated.

sentences.zh: 故管仲曰：『有赦者，奔馬之委轡。

translations.literal: Therefore Guan Zhong said: 'Where there are pardons — a galloping horse casting reins.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said: 'Amnesty is like dropping the reins on a runaway horse.

sentences.zh: 不赦者，痤疽之礪石。

translations.literal: Where there are no pardons — whetstone for boil and carbuncle.'
translations.idiomatic: Refusing pardon is like a whetstone against festering sores.'"

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『惠者，民之仇讐。

translations.literal: " Again he said: 'Favor — the people's enemy-foe.
translations.idiomatic: "He also said: 'Indulgence is the people's enemy.

sentences.zh: 法者，民之父母。

translations.literal: Law — the people's father and mother.'
translations.idiomatic: Law is the people's parent.'"

sentences.zh: 』吳漢遺言，猶云『唯願無赦』。

translations.literal: " Wu Han's dying words still said "only wish there be no amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han's last words likewise were, "I only wish there were no amnesties."

sentences.zh: 王符著論，亦云『赦者非明世之所宜』。

translations.literal: Wang Fu in his treatise also said "amnesty is not what a bright age should employ."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu wrote in his essays as well that amnesties are unsuitable for an enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 豈可數施非常之惠，以肆奸宄之惡乎。

translations.literal: How can one repeatedly grant extraordinary favors to let treacherous villains run wild?
translations.idiomatic: How can the throne repeatedly grant extraordinary indulgence and thereby give free rein to treachery and villainy?

sentences.zh: 」帝亦不納，而昏暴滋甚。

translations.literal: " The emperor likewise did not accept it, and his tyranny grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again refused to listen, and his rule grew ever more brutal and capricious.

sentences.zh: 運乃輿櫬詣朝堂，陳帝八失。

translations.literal: Yun then carried a coffin to the court hall and set forth the emperor's eight failures.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun then came to court bearing a coffin — a sign that he was ready to die — and laid out eight grave failures of the emperor's rule.

sentences.zh: 一曰：內史御正，職在弼諧，皆須參議，共治天下。

translations.literal: First: the inner scribe and rectifier have the duty of assisting and harmonizing; all must join in deliberation and jointly govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: First: the inner scribe and the rectifier exist to assist and harmonize the throne; major affairs should be debated jointly so that all may govern the realm together.

sentences.zh: 大尊比來小大之事，多獨斷之。

translations.literal: Great Esteem of late, in matters great and small, has mostly decided alone.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has decided most matters, great and small, entirely on your own.

sentences.zh: 堯舜至聖，尚資輔弼，比大尊未為聖主，而可專恣己心？

translations.literal: Yao and Shun were supremely sage, yet still relied on assistants; compared with Great Esteem, not yet a sage sovereign — yet may one indulge one's own will?
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao and Shun, the most sage of rulers, relied on advisers; Your Majesty is not yet a sage sovereign — how then can you act entirely as you please?

sentences.zh: 凡諸刑罰爵賞，爰及軍國大事，請參諸宰輔，與眾共之。

translations.literal: For all punishments, rewards of rank, and matters extending to military and state affairs, I beg consultation with the chief ministers and sharing with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: All punishments, enfeoffments, rewards, and military and state affairs should be referred to the chief ministers and decided with their counsel.

sentences.zh: 二曰：內作色荒，古人重誡。

translations.literal: Second: inner indulgence in lust is what the ancients sternly warned against.
translations.idiomatic: Second: to indulge in lust within the palace is what the ancients sternly warned against.

sentences.zh: 大尊初臨四海，德惠未洽，先搜天下美女，用實後宮；

translations.literal: Great Esteem at first facing the four seas, virtue and grace not yet spread, first searched the realm for beautiful women to fill the rear palace;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had barely taken the throne and your virtue had not yet won the realm when you already searched the empire for beautiful women to fill the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 又詔儀同以上女，不許輒嫁。

translations.literal: also ordered that daughters of men of third rank and above were not to be married without permission.
translations.idiomatic: and also decreed that daughters of officials of third rank and above might not marry without permission.

sentences.zh: 貴賤同怨，聲溢朝野。

translations.literal: Noble and common alike resented it; the outcry filled court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: High and low alike resented this, and complaint filled both court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 請姬媵非幸御者，放還本族。

translations.literal: I beg that concubines and attendants not favored for imperial service be sent back to their clans.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that palace women and attendants not actually in Your Majesty's service be released to their families.

sentences.zh: 欲嫁之女，勿更禁之。

translations.literal: Daughters who wish to marry — do not forbid them further.
translations.idiomatic: And for daughters who wish to marry, lift the prohibition.

sentences.zh: 三曰：天子未明求衣，日旰忘食，猶恐萬機不理，天下擁滯。

translations.literal: Third: the Son of Heaven, before dawn seeks clothing, at sunset forgets eating — still fearing the myriad affairs are not managed and the realm is blocked and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Third: a Son of Heaven rises before dawn and forgets to eat until evening, still fearing that the myriad affairs of state will go untended and the realm will stagnate.

sentences.zh: 大尊比來一入後宮，數日不出。

translations.literal: Great Esteem of late, once entering the rear palace, does not emerge for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late enters the inner palace and does not emerge for days on end.

sentences.zh: 所須聞奏，多附內豎。

translations.literal: Matters needing report and memorial mostly pass through inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Business requiring memorials and reports is mostly routed through eunuch attendants.

sentences.zh: 傳言失實，是非可懼。

translations.literal: Rumors miss the truth; right and wrong are fearsome.
translations.idiomatic: Messages passed along in this way lose their truth, and right and wrong become terrifyingly uncertain.

sentences.zh: 事由宦者，亡國之徵。

translations.literal: Affairs handled by eunuchs — a sign of a state's ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When state affairs are handled by eunuchs, that is a sign of dynastic ruin.

sentences.zh: 請准高祖，居外聽政。

translations.literal: I beg following Grand Progenitor, dwelling outside and hearing governance.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty follow Emperor Wu's example and conduct affairs of state outside the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 四曰：變故易常，乃為政之大忌；

translations.literal: Fourth: changing affairs and altering constants is a great taboo in governance;
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: to change established practice and overturn settled norms is among the gravest errors in governance;

sentences.zh: 嚴刑酷罰，非致治之弘規。

translations.literal: harsh punishments and cruel penalties are not the broad standard for bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: and harsh punishments and cruel penalties are not the broad path to good order.

sentences.zh: 若罰無定刑，則天下皆懼；

translations.literal: If punishments have no fixed penalties, then all under Heaven will fear;
translations.idiomatic: If penalties have no fixed standards, everyone under Heaven lives in fear;

sentences.zh: 政無常法，則民無適從。

translations.literal: if governance has no constant law, then the people have nothing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: and if government has no stable law, the people have nothing reliable to follow.

sentences.zh: 豈有削嚴刑之詔未及半祀，便卽追改，更嚴前制？

translations.literal: How can there be an edict reducing harsh punishments not yet half a year old, then immediately reversed and made stricter than before?
translations.idiomatic: How can an edict easing harsh punishments, issued less than half a year ago, be reversed at once and made even harsher than before?

sentences.zh: 政令不定，乃至於是。

translations.literal: Edicts and orders unsettled — it has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Government has reached the point where edicts and orders cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 今宿衛之官，有一人夜不直者，罪至削除；

translations.literal: Now among palace-guard officers, if one man fails night duty, the penalty reaches deprivation of rank;
translations.idiomatic: Now among the palace guard, if a single man misses one night of duty, the penalty is deprivation of rank;

sentences.zh: 因而逃亡者，遂便籍沒。

translations.literal: those who then flee have their households confiscated at once.
translations.idiomatic: and if he then flees, his household is confiscated on the spot.

sentences.zh: 此則大逆之罪，與十杖同科。

translations.literal: This makes the crime of great treason equal in statute to ten strokes of the cane.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the crime of great treason is treated under the same statute as ten strokes of the cane.

sentences.zh: 雖為法愈嚴，恐人情愈散。

translations.literal: Though the law grows ever stricter, I fear hearts grow ever more scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Though the law grows ever harsher, I fear that hearts grow ever more alienated.

sentences.zh: 一人心散，尚或可止，若天下皆散，將如之何。

translations.literal: One person's heart scattered — still perhaps stoppable; if all under Heaven scatter, what then?
translations.idiomatic: When one man's loyalty falters, that may still be checked; but if all under Heaven lose heart, what then can be done?

sentences.zh: 秦網密而國亡，漢章疎而祚永。

translations.literal: Qin's net was dense yet the state perished; Han's statutes were loose yet the throne endured.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's laws were dense and the state perished; Han's statutes were comparatively lenient and the dynasty endured.

sentences.zh: 請遵輕典，竝依大律。

translations.literal: I beg following the lighter canon and all according with the great code.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty follow the lighter standard of law and align punishments with the great code.

sentences.zh: 則億兆之民，手足有所措矣。

translations.literal: Then the hundred million people will have where to set hand and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Then the countless people of the realm will know where they may safely stand.

sentences.zh: 五曰：高祖斲雕為樸，本欲傳之萬世。

translations.literal: Fifth: Grand Progenitor cut carving to make plain, originally intending to transmit it ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: Emperor Wu cut away ornament to restore simplicity, intending that frugality be handed down for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 大尊朝夕趣庭，親承聖旨。

translations.literal: Great Esteem morning and evening hastened to court, personally receiving the sage instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attended court morning and evening and personally received that sage instruction.

sentences.zh: 豈有崩未逾年，而遽窮奢麗，成父之志，義豈然乎。

translations.literal: How can there be, the demise not yet a full year, then suddenly exhausting luxury and splendor — fulfilling the father's will, can the principle be so?
translations.idiomatic: How then, before a full year has passed since his death, can Your Majesty suddenly plunge into extravagance? Would that fulfill your father's intent? Surely not.

sentences.zh: 請興造之制，務從卑儉。

translations.literal: I beg that construction regulations strive for lowliness and thrift.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all building projects be kept humble and frugal.

sentences.zh: 雕文刻鏤，一切勿營。

translations.literal: Carved patterns and inlaid work — do not undertake any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Let there be no carved ornament or inlaid decoration of any kind.

sentences.zh: 六曰：都下之民，徭賦稍重。

translations.literal: Sixth: the people of the capital, corvée and levies are somewhat heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: the people of the capital bear corvée and tax burdens that have grown heavy.

sentences.zh: 必是軍國之要，不敢憚勞。

translations.literal: Surely it is for military and state necessity; they dare not shrink from toil.
translations.idiomatic: If the need were truly military or fiscal, they would not shrink from the labor.

sentences.zh: 豈容朝夕徵求，唯供魚龍爛漫，士民從役，祇為俳優角抵。

translations.literal: How can one tolerate daily levies morning and evening, solely to supply aquatic and dragon spectacles; scholars and commoners in service only for entertainers and wrestling?
translations.idiomatic: But how can daily exactions be tolerated when they serve only aquatic pageants and dragon displays, and when scholars and commoners are conscripted solely for acrobats and wrestlers?

sentences.zh: 紛紛不已，財力俱竭，業業相顧，無復聊生。

translations.literal: Unceasing turmoil; wealth and strength both exhausted; trembling and looking at one another — no longer any livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Such demands go on without end; wealth and strength are exhausted; people tremble and stare at one another, with no means left to live.

sentences.zh: 凡此無益之事，請並停罷。

translations.literal: For all such useless matters, I beg they all be stopped and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All such useless undertakings should be stopped at once.

sentences.zh: 七曰：近見有詔，上書字誤者，卽治其罪。

translations.literal: Seventh: recently there was seen an edict that whoever errs in characters in a memorial is immediately punished for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: recently an edict appeared stating that anyone who makes a written error in a memorial is to be punished immediately.

sentences.zh: 假有忠讜之人，欲陳時事，尺有所短，文字非工，不密失身，義無假手，脫有舛謬，便陷嚴科。

translations.literal: Suppose there is a loyal and forthright man wishing to set forth current affairs — the foot has its short measure, writing is not his craft; not careful he loses his person, in principle no one to lend a hand; if there be slip or error, he falls into harsh statute.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose a loyal and outspoken man wishes to address current affairs: everyone has his limits, and writing may not be his strength; if he cannot be careful he risks his life, and he has no one to draft the words for him — the slightest slip will bring him under harsh penalty.

sentences.zh: 嬰徑尺之鱗，其事非易，下不諱之詔，猶懼未來，更加刑戮，能無鉗口！

translations.literal: Ying the giant fish of a foot's width — the matter is not easy; an edict that faults are not tabooed — still one fears it will not come; add further punishments and executions — can mouths not be clamped shut!
translations.idiomatic: To kill the giant fish of Handan is no easy thing; even an edict promising that faults need not be concealed still leaves men afraid for the future — add executions on top of that, and who will not fall silent?

sentences.zh: 大尊縱不能采誹謗之言，無宜杜獻書之路。

translations.literal: Great Esteem even if unable to accept slanderous words, should not block the road of submitting writings.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty cannot accept harsh criticism, you should not close the path by which memorials reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 請停此詔，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg stopping this edict — then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this edict be withdrawn; then all under Heaven would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 八曰：昔桑穀生朝，殷王因之獲福。

translations.literal: Eighth: formerly mulberry and grain grew in the court; the king of Yin thereby obtained blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: in antiquity mulberry and grain sprouted in the royal court, and the Yin king turned the omen into a blessing.

sentences.zh: 今玄象垂誡，此亦興周之祥。

translations.literal: Now dark signs hang as warning — this too is an auspice for Zhou's rise.
translations.idiomatic: Now celestial signs warn from above — this too may be an auspice for Zhou's renewal.

sentences.zh: 大尊雖減膳撤懸，未盡銷譴之理。

translations.literal: Great Esteem though reducing meals and removing suspended instruments, has not fully exhausted the principle of dispelling reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reduced your meals and removed court music, yet has not fully done what is needed to answer Heaven's reproof.

sentences.zh: 誠願諮諏善道，修布德政，解兆民之慍，引萬方之罪，則天變可除，鼎業方固。

translations.literal: Truly I wish consulting on the good Way, cultivating and spreading virtuous governance, releasing the anger of the hundred million people, drawing the blame of the ten thousand directions — then heavenly changes can be removed and the tripod enterprise be made firm.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope Your Majesty will seek good counsel, spread virtuous rule, ease the anger of the people, and take upon yourself the blame of the realm — then heavenly warnings may be dispelled and the dynasty made secure.

sentences.zh: 大尊若不革茲八事，臣見周廟不血食矣。

translations.literal: Great Esteem if not reforming these eight matters, your servant sees Zhou temples receiving no blood sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not reform these eight matters, I foresee the temples of Zhou receiving no sacrifices at all.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，將戮之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 內史元巌紿帝曰：「樂運知書奏必死，所以不顧身命者，欲取後世之名。

translations.literal: Inner Scribe Yuwen Yuan deceived the emperor, saying: "Yue Yun knows that submitting this memorial means certain death; the reason he does not spare his body and life is that he wishes to win a name for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Scribe Yuwen Yuan said to the emperor, "Yue Yun knew this memorial would mean his death; he risked his life only to win a name for posterity.

sentences.zh: 陛下若殺之，乃成其名也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty kills him, you will have made his name."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty executes him, you will only make that name immortal."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，因而獲免。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented to this and thereby he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the point and Yue Yun was spared.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝頗感悟。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor was somewhat moved to reflection.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor was somewhat moved by reflection.

sentences.zh: 召運謂之曰：「朕昨夜思卿所奏，寔是忠臣。

translations.literal: He summoned Yun and said to him: "Last night I considered what you memorialized — truly a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yue Yun and said, "Last night I considered your memorial — you are truly a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 先皇明聖，卿數有規諫。

translations.literal: The late emperor was bright and sage; you several times had remonstrance and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was wise and sage, and you remonstrated with him many times.

sentences.zh: 朕旣昏暗，卿復能如此。

translations.literal: I am already benighted; you again were able to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: I am benighted by comparison, yet you were still able to speak as you did."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜御食以賞之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed imperial food to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded him with food from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 朝之公卿，初見帝盛怒，莫不為運寒心。

translations.literal: The court's dukes and ministers, at first seeing the emperor's great anger, all feared for Yun's heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first saw the emperor's fury, every minister feared for Yue Yun's life.

sentences.zh: 後見獲宥，皆相賀以為倖免虎口。

translations.literal: Later seeing him spared, all congratulated one another as having escaped the tiger's mouth.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw him spared, they congratulated one another on his escape from the tiger's jaws.

sentences.zh: 內史鄭譯嘗以私事請託運而弗之許，因此銜之。

translations.literal: Inner Scribe Zheng Yi once asked Yun to grant a private favor and he did not permit it; for this Yi harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Scribe Zheng Yi once asked Yue Yun for a private favor, which he refused; Zheng Yi therefore nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及隋文帝為丞相，譯為長史，遂左遷運為廣州滍陽令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister and Yi was chief clerk, he then demoted Yun to magistrate of Zhiyang in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chief minister and Zheng Yi served as his chief clerk, Yue Yun was demoted to magistrate of Zhiyang in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，轉毛州高唐令。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang, transferred to magistrate of Gaotang in Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was transferred to magistrate of Gaotang in Maozhou.

sentences.zh: 頻歷二縣，竝有聲績。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly served two counties, both had reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He served two counties in succession and won a good reputation in both.

sentences.zh: 運常願處一諫官，從容諷議。

translations.literal: Yun always wished to hold a remonstrance office and calmly offer admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun always hoped to hold a remonstrance office where he could offer calm, measured counsel.

sentences.zh: 而性訐直，為人所排抵，遂不被任用。

translations.literal: But his nature was blunt and straight; men pushed against him, and he was not employed.
translations.idiomatic: But his nature was blunt and uncompromising; others blocked him, and he was never given such a post.

sentences.zh: 乃發憤，錄夏殷以來諫諍事，集而部之，凡六百三十九條，合四十一卷，名曰《諫苑》。

translations.literal: Thereupon in indignation he recorded remonstrance affairs from Xia and Yin onward, collected and arranged them — in all six hundred thirty-nine entries, forty-one scrolls total, titled Garden of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: In frustration he then compiled cases of remonstrance from the Xia and Yin dynasties onward: six hundred thirty-nine entries in forty-one scrolls, entitled Garden of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 奏上之。

translations.literal: He submitted it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the work to the throne.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝覽而嘉焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui read it and praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：士有不因學藝而重，不待爵祿而貴者何？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Are there gentlemen who are honored without relying on learning and arts, ennobled without waiting for rank and salary?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Are there men honored without relying on learning, ennobled without waiting for rank and salary?

sentences.zh: 亦云忠孝而已。

translations.literal: One may say it is loyalty and filial piety alone.
translations.idiomatic: One may say that it is loyalty and filial piety alone.

sentences.zh: 若乃竭力以奉其親者，人子之行也；

translations.literal: If one exhausts strength to serve one's parents — that is a son's conduct;
translations.idiomatic: To exhaust oneself in serving one's parents is the conduct of a son;

sentences.zh: 致身以事其君者，人臣之節也。

translations.literal: to give body to serve one's lord — that is a minister's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: to give body and life in serving one's lord is the integrity of a minister.

sentences.zh: 斯固彌綸三極，囊括百代。

translations.literal: This indeed spans the three poles and embraces a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: These virtues indeed bind heaven, earth, and man and embrace every age.

sentences.zh: 當宣帝之在東朝，凶德方兆，王軌、宇文孝伯、神舉志惟無隱，盡言於父子之間。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was in the Eastern Palace, vicious virtue was just appearing; Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and Shenju's intent was only not to hide — speaking fully between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was crown prince and his vicious character was already showing, Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and Yuwen Shenju resolved to hide nothing and spoke plainly between father and son.

sentences.zh: 淫刑旣逞，相繼夷滅。

translations.literal: Once licentious punishments were unleashed, they were successively exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Once cruel punishments were unleashed, they were destroyed one after another.

sentences.zh: 隋文之將登庸，人懷去就。

translations.literal: When Sui Wen was about to take power, men harbored thoughts of staying or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was about to seize power, men everywhere weighed whether to stay or flee.

sentences.zh: 顏之儀風烈懍然，正辭以明節，崎嶇雷電之下，僅而獲濟。

translations.literal: Yan Zhiyi's bearing was stern and awe-inspiring; with upright words he clarified integrity; under thunder and lightning in hardship, barely obtained deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiyi stood with stern, awe-inspiring bearing, spoke with upright words to declare his integrity, and barely survived the storm when power changed hands.

sentences.zh: 斯數子者，豈非社稷之臣歟。

translations.literal: These several men — are they not ministers of the altars of soil and grain?
translations.idiomatic: Were these men not true pillars of the state?

sentences.zh: 或人以為不忠，則天下莫之信也。

translations.literal: If some say they were disloyal, then none under Heaven would believe it.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone called them disloyal, no one under Heaven would believe it.

sentences.zh: 自古以外戚而居重任，多藉一時之恩，至若尉遲運者，可謂位以才升，爵由功進。

translations.literal: From antiquity, those related by marriage who held heavy responsibility mostly relied on a moment's favor; as for Wei Chiyun, one may say rank rose through talent, title advanced through merit.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, in-laws who held high office have mostly owed their place to a moment's favor; but Wei Chiyun may be said to have risen by talent and advanced by merit.

sentences.zh: 美矣哉。

translations.literal: How beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Truly admirable!

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
